title: Federal Heat Pump Rebate: Who Gets $10,000 or $2,000 (2026)
desc: Canada's federal heat pump rebate: $10,000 at or below your province's income line, $2,000 above it. Income table, gas homes, rentals, Nov 1 installs, March 2034 end.
h1: Canada's National Heat Pump Rebate: Who Qualifies and How It Works
badge: Up to $10,000, or $2,000 for most homeowners
lead: Ottawa has now published who qualifies. You get up to $10,000 if your after-tax household income is at or below your province's line, and $2,000 if it is above. Homes heated with gas, oil, propane, electricity or wood can apply, and so can rental properties you own. The portal opens in early 2027, and installs from November 1, 2026 can apply once it does. Ottawa says details can still change, so we re-read its page often and show the date.
cards_heading: The federal rebate at a glance
cards_intro: Every figure below comes from the Government of Canada's own campaign page, which we re-read in full on November 19, 2026. Ottawa says the rules are still being finalized, so we show the date we checked.

cards.title: Households below the median income
cards.note: For a cold climate heat pump. Your after-tax household income must be at or below the line for your province and household size (table below). The Canada Revenue Agency checks it with your Social Insurance Number.

cards.title: Other eligible homeowners
cards.note: Flat amount for eligible homeowners above the income line. One rebate per household, even if you own more than one property.

cards.title: When it starts and ends
cards.note: The portal opens in early 2027. Installs from November 1, 2026 can apply once it opens. No money is paid before launch. The program closes in March 2034.

cards.title: Combine with provincial rebates
cards.note: The government says the rebates can be combined with provincial programs. Each province still has its own rules, so we check them one by one.

cards.title: Free retrofit for lower incomes
cards.note: The older Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program installs insulation and heat pumps at no cost for low-to-median-income homeowners and tenants. It is open in BC, Manitoba, Nova Scotia, PEI and Quebec.

cards.title: Apartment buildings
cards.note: Separate CMHC, Canada Infrastructure Bank and Deep Retrofit Accelerator money is aimed at rental buildings, not at individual tenants.

after_cards: The government says the program can reach up to 820,000 households. For homes heating with oil, propane or electric resistance it quotes average savings of more than $1,400 a year. For natural gas homes it warns that switching may not lower your bills, depending on your region and system. We cover that in heat pump on a natural gas home.
sections: Which tier do you get? The income table

The $10,000 rebate is for households with after-tax income at or below the line for their province or territory and household size. Ottawa uses median after-tax household income from the 2021 Census, in 2025 dollars. Your income is line 23600 (net income) minus line 43500 (total taxes payable) on your 2025 tax return, plus your spouse's or partner's if you have one. The government checks it with the Canada Revenue Agency when you apply. Above the line, you get $2,000.

How it works, step by step

Ottawa says there is no energy audit before or after the install.

  1. You buy and install a heat pump from the eligible product list. Systems are listed by AHRI number, and the heat pump must be sold and installed by an HVAC contractor.
  2. The system should heat the whole home. Ask your contractor to confirm it is sized for the house.
  3. When the portal opens in early 2027, you apply online. For the higher rebate you give your Social Insurance Number.
  4. You upload receipts within 6 months. They must show your name and address, the installing company, the make, model and AHRI number, how many heat pumps, and the total project cost, including ductwork and electrical work directly tied to the install.
  5. Ottawa's October 8 release said approval within 24 hours and payment within five days by direct deposit. The campaign page does not repeat those timings.

You do not have to remove your old system or show it broke down. Emergency and planned installs both count.

• Changes. The campaign page says parameters and eligibility are still being finalized and can change. Rules are judged on the date you install.
  • Installs before November 1, 2026. The page says nothing about them.
  • Rented or leased heat pumps. They may be eligible after launch, with details later.
  • Remote areas. Ottawa notes there may be few certified installers.
  • Condos and tenants. You must own the home. See renters, condos and landlords.

When any of this changes, we update this page with the source and date.
Why the quote matters more than the rebate

Many homeowners worry that contractors raise prices by the amount of any rebate. Whether or not that happens near you, you can protect yourself by getting a written load calculation, three itemized quotes and a price for the same equipment with and without the rebate. Our guide on how to get a fair heat pump quote walks through it.
Should you wait or buy now?

If your system still works, waiting a few months costs little and lets you see the real rules. If it has failed and you need heat this winter, provincial money available today may be worth more than a federal rebate that is not open yet. We lay out the deadlines in Should you wait for the federal heat pump rebate?

The federal money is meant to sit on top of provincial programs. Here is what is live today, each from the program's own page.

  • British Columbia: BC Hydro pays up to $4,000 for a whole-home heat pump replacing electric heat. CleanBC pays $13,000, $7,000 or $3,500 by income level for gas, propane or oil homes. See the BC hub.
  • Ontario: Home Renovation Savings pays $1,250 per ton up to $7,500 for homes heated with electricity, oil, propane or wood, and $500 per ton up to $2,000 for gas homes. See the Ontario hub.
  • Nova Scotia: Efficiency Nova Scotia pays per ton, and HomeWarming installs upgrades free for lower incomes. See the Nova Scotia hub.
  • Alberta: we found no province-wide heat pump rebate, and the earlier federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability program closed on July 31, 2026, so the new federal rebate may matter most here. See the Alberta hub.

The full breakdown, with sample stacks, is in federal and provincial heat pump rebates: what stacks.
claim_heading: What to do before the rebate launches
claim_steps: Sign up for updates on the Canada.ca campaign page, and for our launch-day email below.
Find your province's income line in the table and work out your household's after-tax income from your 2025 tax return.
Check the eligible product list (AHRI number) before you accept a quote.
Ask your installer for a written heat load calculation and an itemized quote that lists the make, model and AHRI number.
If you install after November 1, 2026, keep the invoice and receipts and submit them within 6 months of launch.
Check your province's live rebate and its deadline on your province hub, and run your numbers in our rebate calculator.

faq: How much is the National Heat Pump Rebate?
$10,000 if your after-tax household income is at or below your province's line for your household size, and $2,000 if it is above. The actual amount also depends on your equipment cost.
How do I know if I get $10,000 or $2,000?

Compare your after-tax household income (line 23600 minus line 43500 on your 2025 tax return, plus a partner's) with the table on this page. The Canada Revenue Agency checks it through your Social Insurance Number when you apply.
When can I apply?
The portal opens in early 2027. No money is paid before launch. Sign up for the Canada.ca updates and our launch-day email.
When does the federal heat pump rebate end?
Ottawa says the program closes in March 2034.
Will it cover a heat pump I install now?
Ottawa says installs from November 1, 2026 can apply once the portal opens. It says nothing about earlier installs. Submit receipts within 6 months and keep your invoice.
Does a natural gas home qualify?
Yes. Homes heated with electricity, natural gas, oil, propane, diesel, coal or wood can apply. Ottawa warns that switching from gas may not lower your bills in every region.
Does a rental property qualify?
Yes if you own it and live in Canada. The home does not need to be your main home. You get one rebate per household, even with several properties.
Can I combine it with BC Hydro, Home Renovation Savings or Efficiency Nova Scotia?
The government says the rebate can be combined with provincial programs. Each provincial program has its own rules, so confirm with the program before you buy.
Do I need an energy audit?
No. Ottawa says no audit is needed before or after the install. Some provincial programs still ask for one, such as the Ontario assessment stream.
Is this the same as the Canada Greener Homes Grant?
No. The old Greener Homes Grant is closed. The Greener Homes Affordability Program is a separate free-retrofit program for lower incomes, and this is a new rebate.
